original_query: select  i_item_id,         ca_country,         ca_state,         ca_county,         avg( cast(cs_quantity as decimal(12,2))) agg1,         avg( cast(cs_list_price as decimal(12,2))) agg2,         avg( cast(cs_coupon_amt as decimal(12,2))) agg3,         avg( cast(cs_sales_price as decimal(12,2))) agg4,         avg( cast(cs_net_profit as decimal(12,2))) agg5,         avg( cast(c_birth_year as decimal(12,2))) agg6 from catalog_sales, customer_demographics, customer, customer_address, date_dim, item where cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and       cs_item_sk = i_item_sk and       cs_bill_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and       cs_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk and       cd_gender = 'F' and       cd_education_status = 'College' and       c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk and       d_year = 1999 and       c_birth_month = 5 and       ca_state in ('IN', 'MI', 'WI')       and cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 69 AND 74       AND i_category = 'Sports'  group by rollup (i_item_id, ca_country, ca_state, ca_county)  order by ca_country,         ca_state,         ca_county, 	i_item_id  limit 100;
rewritten_query:
select i_item_id,
       ca_country,
       ca_state,
       ca_county,
       avg(cast(cs_quantity as decimal(12,2))) agg1,
       avg(cast(cs_list_price as decimal(12,2))) agg2,
       avg(cast(cs_coupon_amt as decimal(12,2))) agg3,
       avg(cast(cs_sales_price as decimal(12,2))) agg4,
       avg(cast(cs_net_profit as decimal(12,2))) agg5,
       avg(cast(c_birth_year as decimal(12,2))) agg6
from catalog_sales cs
join date_dim d on cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
join item i on cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
join customer_demographics cd on cs.cs_bill_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
join customer c on cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
join customer_address ca on c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
where d.d_year = 1999
  and i.i_category = 'Sports'
  and cd.cd_gender = 'F'
  and cd.cd_education_status = 'College'
  and c.c_birth_month = 5
  and ca.ca_state in ('IN', 'MI', 'WI')
  and cs.cs_wholesale_cost between 69 and 74
group by rollup (i.i_item_id, ca.ca_country, ca.ca_state, ca.ca_county)
order by ca.ca_country,
         ca.ca_state,
         ca.ca_county,
         i.i_item_id
limit 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Converted implicit comma-separated joins into explicit INNER JOIN syntax with table aliases, improving readability and making join conditions explicit. All filter predicates (d_year, i_category, cd_gender, cd_education_status, c_birth_month, ca_state, cs_wholesale_cost) are kept in the WHERE clause; the optimizer pushes them down to the dimension scans.

All selective predicates are already simple equality/IN/BETWEEN filters on dimension attributes; no redundant or contradictory predicates exist to remove. The ROLLUP grouping and LIMIT 100 require computing all groups before sort, so no further predicate restructuring is beneficial.
No subqueries or CTEs are present. Creating CTEs is not recommended: there are no redundant subquery calculations, and CTE materialization could hurt performance (especially on PostgreSQL <12).

Join order is left to the optimizer. The existing plan uses the index on catalog_sales(cs_bill_customer_sk) with nested loops from the selective customer birth-month filter, which is reasonable. Optionally consider a composite index catalog_sales(cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_wholesale_cost) (or one on cs_sold_date_sk) if EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows heavy heap access on catalog_sales.

Constants (1999, 'F', 'College', 5, ('IN','MI','WI'), 69–74, 'Sports') are already literal and will be folded/pushed by the planner. Per-row casts to decimal(12,2) were retained to preserve exact output type/semantics of the original query.
